title: The friend invite page is never tested for a member with no first name
what: Every invite-page test uses an inviter called Asha. Nothing checks the 'A friend invited you' and 'Your friend does not' wording, or that the word 'undefined' never shows.
expected: A test opens an invite from a member with no first name and checks the friendly wording and that the send still works.
fix_line: Add one invite-page test with an empty inviter name

title: The join page keeps the person's name and checked number in the browser tab, and the test expects it to
what: The join-online test reloads the page half-way and after sending, and checks the name and checked number come back. The journey says the number must not be kept by the page itself.
expected: Either the journey allows tab-only keeping until the tab closes, or the page forgets the number after sending; the test then checks whichever is decided.
who: people joining online on a shared phone
fix_line: Decide the rule, then make the page and its test match

title: The join page's refusal and change messages are never seen by a test
what: No screen test checks 'Too many sign-ups were sent today...', 'Use another number', 'Change number', 'Step 1 of 3', or what happens when the gym's plan or price changes while the page is open.
expected: A screen test covers each of these messages and the plan-changed path, and checks 'Sent to <gym>' stays hidden after a refusal.
fix_line: Add screen tests for the daily limit, plan changed and the two buttons

title: How long the update notes are kept is never tested
what: The update-notes address tests check the status codes only. Nothing checks the 10-minute keep time, the 1-minute time on a kept copy, that a failure is never kept, or that a second request skips GitHub.
expected: Tests check the keep times on each answer and that a kept copy is used without asking GitHub again.
fix_line: Assert the cache headers and a cache hit in the existing test file

title: The update screen promises up to 5 new lines, but the app keeps only 3
what: The journey says the full-screen update shows up to 5 What's new lines. The app's own test checks it reads at most 3 lines and drops the rest.
expected: The journey and the app agree on one number, and the test checks that number.
fix_line: Pick 3 or 5 and fix the journey or the app to match

title: When saving feedback fails, people see the offline words, not 'Could not save. Try again.'
what: The tests check that a failed save shows the app's offline words ("Couldn't send"), while the journey expects 'Could not save. Try again.'.
expected: One wording for a failed save, written into both the journey and the tests.
fix_line: Choose the words and update the journey or the apps

title: The get-the-app page on a computer is checked only for its blocks, not its words or QR
what: The test checks the computer page has a QR block and the two store names. It never checks the headline, the 'Scan this QR code' line, 'Coming soon', or that the QR points at the app link.
expected: A test checks the words and decodes or reads the QR's address.
who: people getting the app from a computer
fix_line: Check the page words and the QR target in the existing test

title: The help box's daily message limit is never tested
what: Feedback's daily limit is tested, but the help box (which answers questions) has no test that the limit refuses a question and gives no AI answer.
expected: A test sends questions past the daily limit and checks 'Too many messages today' with no AI call.
who: owners, staff and members asking for help
fix_line: Add a limit test to the help tests
